To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a human monoclonal stomach carcinoma-specific antibody induces apoptosis and can be used for adjuvanticum therapy of stomach carcinoma.

the human antibody SC-1 can induce a significant apoptosis in stomach carcinoma cells, and that this antibody has been successfully applied in a phase I trial for the treatment of poorly differentiated stomach carcinoma.
the human monocional antibody SC-1 induces apoptosis of stomach-carcinomas by binding a stomach carcinoma-associated isoform of the complement regulator CD55/DAf.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new strategies in the adjuvant treatment of stomach carcinoma, based on tumor-specific monoclonal antibodies.
the development of a new type of immunotherapy of stomach cancer, which is directed against the specific tumor antigen CD55/DAFB and which can be used in a curative setting.
the development of new therapeutic strategies against cancer, especially stomach carcinoma, by using monoclonal antibodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SC-1 antibody has a high potential for the treatment of stomach carcinoma.
the SC-1 antibody is a very promising new tool for adjuvant immunotherapy in patients with stomach carcinoma.
SC-1 is a promising new adjuvant therapy of stomach carcinoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we could demonstrate the induction of apoptosis by the antibody SC-1 in stomach carcinoma cells in vitro and in patients in vivo.
we have shown that SC-1 antibody can be successfully used in patients with stomach carcinoma for adjuvant immunotherapy.
the SC-1 antibody is a promising tool for adjuvant treatment of stomach carcinoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now identify the most promising targets for the development of novel therapies.
it is possible to use a human antibody to induce apoptosis of human cancer cells in vivo and that this approach is clinically feasible.
the use of the SC1 antibody in the adjuvant therapy setting can be a safe and effective treatment modality for gastric cancer.
